publication: Scott Aaronson, The Busy Beaver Frontier, SIGACT News 51(3):31–55, 2020, as listed by the author. Inspected official 24-page manuscript.

reviews.checked_passages: Root source selection on 2026-11-09: manuscript sections1–2, pp1–5, definitions of state-count and language-description variants, full Propositions1–2 and their proofs. Adjacent Proposition3 and its arguments were read for the scope boundary but are excluded from adoption. Author paper listing confirmed the journal details.
reviews.consumers: busy-beaver-functions, especially finite-contestants, busy-beaver-bounds, short-constant-programs, dominates-computable-functions and halting-equivalence.
reviews.outcome: No confirmed defect in the selected adopted passages. The corpus develops an explicit syntax-node variant in the existing recursive-program language, finite candidate enumeration and binary constant compiler, with exact size and evaluation identities. Its resource bound concerns successful bounded-evaluator allowances, not tape transition counts. Output-oracle recovery of halting uses a separate resource-witness compiler. These expanded implementations are corpus arguments; numeric record values, sound-theory independence and higher oracle variants are excluded.
